openFindings.title: A SIGHUP, SIGTERM or parent-death stop leaves every lineage open in the ledger, so the next run requeues each as an orphan and charges it a retry
--stop signals the process group of whatever process now holds a ledger pid, with no check it is still a lineage
Lineage block written only after the lineage exits, so a resumed research lineage scopes events under a second lineage id
A lineage that omits timestamp on its iteration records escapes every stamp check the fan-out runs
The packet every range commit cites records none of the fan-out trust, stop or blocked-stop work
Three copies of the claimed-stamp choice use two different predicates
One ledger event name, stopped, carries two shapes and only the label tells them apart, so --status shows a SIGHUP-stopped run as running
Blocked-stop event reports every active finding as adjudicated, even when the claim-adjudication gate is the blocker
The documented review blocked_stop row is not the projected row, and the skipped-gate unknown never reaches the state log
Research blocked-stop row hard-codes hotspotSaturation pass:true while the review side reports an unevaluated gate as unknown
One attempt log with no timed event turns every pass of the lineage to unknown, including a later timed attempt's passes
The 20 MB stdout cap that kills a lineage now counts the full claude stream-json transcript, tool results included

nodes.question: Fan-out trust: does the per-pass evidence (examined/unexamined flags) judge a lineage pass correctly, does the lineage timestamp window use the gateway clock and claimedTimestamp, and is the runner-written lineage block in each lineage config right?
Stop and kill: do --stop, SIGHUP and parent death stop every lineage process and record a stopped outcome with a rerun command, and does --status show live progress rows read-only?
Blocked stop and dry run: does convergence.cjs record a blocked stop from the script with skipped gates as unknown, and do both workflows keep that call read-only on a dry run?
Do rotated lineage logs (fanout-lineage.N.out) mixing a timed and an untimed attempt leave pass windows judged against the wrong attempt's calls?
